title: A principal completion detects good properties near the closed fibre
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative quasi-excellent ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], let $t\in C$, and let $B=\widehat C_{(t)}$ with its canonical map from $C$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume $B$ is reduced, meaning $b^n=0$ for $n\geq1$ implies $b=0$, multiplication by $t$ on $B$ is injective, and $B[1/t]$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then there exists $g\in1+tC$ such that $A=C_g$ is reduced, multiplication by $t$ on $A$ is injective, and $A[1/t]$ is regular. Here $C_g$ and $B[1/t]$ are localizations at the respective powers of $g$ and $t$. The canonical map $\widehat C_{(t)}\to\widehat{C_g}_{(t)}$ is an isomorphism. Thus the replacement preserves the distinguished generator and every quotient by its positive powers.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.5(ii), the reducedness comparison following it (printed p.18), and the shrinking in the proof of Theorem 3.4.1 (printed p.22); the injectivity condition is treated by the finite module ker(t:C -> C). Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [def-exc-excellent-ring], $C$ is Noetherian and J-2. Thus every ideal of $C$ is finite [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a closed subset $V(I)$ for some ideal $I$: apply J-2 to the finite type $C$-algebra $C$ itself. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], $B$ is Noetherian and $C\to B$ is flat. These facts do not require the completion map to be faithfully flat.

source.place: Tags 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian), 00MB(1) (lemma-completion-flat); more-algebra.tex Tag 07P7 (definition-J), used through the stated J-2 definition.

proof.text: Let $N=\{x\in C:x^n=0\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$ and $T=\ker(t:C\to C)$. They are finite ideals. Completing $0\to M\to C\to C/M\to0$, for $M=N,T$, gives an injection $\widehat M\to B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules]. For $M=N$, [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] identifies its image with the ideal generated by the images of $N$ in $B$; each such image is nilpotent and hence zero because $B$ is reduced. For $M=T$, the composite of this injection with multiplication by $t$ is zero, by the coordinatewise formula for completed maps, and injectivity of $t$ on $B$ again makes the image zero. Hence $\widehat N=\widehat T=0$. The surjective first projections of [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] give $N/tN=T/tT=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] to obtain $h_N,h_T\in1+tC$ with $h_NN=h_TT=0$.

Set $J=\{x\in C:t^nx\in I\text{ for some }n\geq0\}$, the saturation of $I$ by powers of $t$. This is an ideal, since exponents can be increased to a common exponent; it contains $I$. Multiplication by $t$ on $D=C/J$ is injective: $tx\in J$ implies $t^{n+1}x\in I$ for some $n$, hence $x\in J$. The ideal $J$ is finite by Noetherianity. Completing $0\to J\to C\to D\to0$ and using the tensor description of $\widehat J$ identifies $\widehat D$ canonically with $R=B/JB$, by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] and [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor]. Completing $0\to D\xrightarrow{t}D\to D/tD\to0$ by the same exactness node shows that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective. All modules in these two sequences are finite over the Noetherian ring $C$.

source.place: Tags 00MA(3) (lemma-completion-tensor) and 00MB(2) (lemma-completion-flat); saturation is the explicit elementary ideal argument given here.

proof.text: Every prime of $R$ contains $t$. Indeed, otherwise its inverse image $\mathfrak q$ in $B$ contains $JB$ and avoids $t$. Its contraction $\mathfrak p$ in $C$ contains $J\supseteq I$, so $C_{\mathfrak p}$ is not regular by the choice of $I$. On the other hand $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring: it is the same ring of fractions as the local ring of $B[1/t]$ at the prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q$, and $B[1/t]$ is regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], the flat map $C\to B$ induces a flat local map $C_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ of Noetherian local rings. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] to conclude that $C_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular, a contradiction.

source.place: Tags 00HT(6) (lemma-flat-localization) and 00OF (lemma-flat-under-regular); the two successive localizations are identified by their fraction formulas.

proof.text: The affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply part (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-kernel-image-ideal] with $\mathcal B=\mathcal E=\mathcal O_X$ and $e$ multiplication by $t$. It gives the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal K=(t)\mathcal O_X$, with $\mathcal K(X)=tR$. It is of finite type because $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal K$, $a\mapsto ta$, is locally surjective [pqf-def-coherent]. Its vanishing set is $X$: at every prime, $t$ is in the maximal ideal of the local ring by Step 4, so cannot generate the unit ideal. Thus [lemma-nagata-finite-type-nil-ideal-nilpotent] gives $t^eR=0$ for some $e>0$. As multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective by Step 3, iterated cancellation gives $R=0$. Consequently $\widehat D=0$, and the surjective first projection of [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] gives $D/tD=0$. Equivalently $J+tC=C$. Write $1=j+tc$ with $j\in J$, and put $h_J=j=1-tc\in1+tC$. By the definition of $J$ there is $n\geq0$ with $t^nh_J\in I$.

source.place: Statement, applied to the principal ideal (t); Stacks algebra.tex Tags 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact), 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated); quasi-coherent generated ideals through the cited generic algebra-sheaf node.

proof.text: Set $g=h_Nh_Th_J\in1+tC$ and $A=C_g$. Each factor is invertible in $A$. If $(x/g^r)^m=0$, there is $k\geq0$ with $g^kx^m=0$; then $y=g^kx$ is nilpotent, so $h_Ny=0$ and hence $x/g^r=0$. Thus $A$ is reduced. If $t(x/g^r)=0$, choose $k$ with $tg^kx=0$; then $g^kx\in T$, so $h_Tg^kx=0$ and again $x/g^r=0$. Thus $t$ acts injectively on $A$. Finally $t^nh_J\in I$ becomes a unit in $A[1/t]$, so every prime of $C$ avoiding $gt$ avoids $I$. Its local ring is regular by the definition of $V(I)$. The local rings of $C[1/(gt)]=A[1/t]$ are those same local rings, by the fraction formulas. This ring is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], so it is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), localization clause; Tag 00OD (definition-regular); the reducedness and torsion assertions are the displayed fraction arguments.

proof.text: Write $g=1+tu$. For each $r\geq1$ the image of $g$ in $C/t^rC$ has inverse $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(-tu)^i$. Therefore the quotient map induces an isomorphism $C/t^rC\to C_g/t^rC_g$; explicitly its inverse sends $x/g^m$ to $x(\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(-tu)^i)^m\bmod t^r$. These isomorphisms commute with quotient transitions, because they all extend the same map from $C$ and send $g^{-1}$ to the unique inverse of $g$. Taking the compatible sequences gives an isomorphism $\widehat C_{(t)}\to\widehat{C_g}_{(t)}$, with inverse defined coordinatewise by the displayed formula [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It is the canonical completion map and sends the image of $t$ to the image of $t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], the corresponding positive-power quotients of both completions are precisely the original quotients, with their canonical projections. Thus all the stated quotient and generator identifications are preserved.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), ring case; the isomorphism is the explicit geometric-sum inverse on each quotient.

lean.statement: theorem exists_goodNeighborhood_of_principalCompletion (C : Type u) [CommRing C] (hC : IsQuasiExcellent C) (t : C) (hred : IsReduced (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {t}) C)) (ht : Function.Injective (fun b : AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {t}) C ↦ algebraMap C (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {t}) C) t * b)) (hreg : IsRegularRing (Localization.Away (algebraMap C (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {t}) C) t))) : ∃ g : C, (∃ c : C, g = 1 + t * c) ∧ IsReduced (Localization.Away g) ∧ Function.Injective (fun a : Localization.Away g ↦ algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) t * a) ∧ IsRegularRing (Localization.Away (algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) t)) ∧ ∃ E : AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {t}) C ≃+* AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) t}) (Localization.Away g), (∀ c : C, E (algebraMap C (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {t}) C) c) = algebraMap (Localization.Away g) (AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) t}) (Localization.Away g)) (algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) c)) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ e : (C ⧸ (Ideal.span {t}) ^ n) ≃+* ((Localization.Away g) ⧸ (Ideal.span {algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) t}) ^ n), (∀ c : C, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((Ideal.span {t}) ^ n) c) = Ideal.Quotient.mk ((Ideal.span {algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) t}) ^ n) (algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) c)) ∧ ∀ b : AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {t}) C, AdicCompletion.evalₐ (Ideal.span {algebraMap C (Localization.Away g) t}) n (E b) = e (AdicCompletion.evalₐ (Ideal.span {t}) n b)
